comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C17-C19 regarding Swi4 downregulation during meiotic entry. Both evaluations find the immunoblotting data (Figure 1B-C) convincing and support the differential regulation of SBF/MBF subunits.

Perfect agreement on claims C20-C21 regarding differential expression patterns of SBF vs MBF targets. Both accept the RNA-seq data (Figure 1D) demonstrating functional specialization during meiosis vs mitosis.

Strong agreement on claims C22-C26 regarding selective SBF activation. OpenEval evaluates these claims separately, while peer review groups them with C27-C28 (meiotic entry delay). Both find the overexpression experiments convincing.

Agreement on claims C27-C28 regarding meiotic entry delay from SWI4 overexpression. OpenEval evaluates these separately while peer review groups them with C22-C26. Both accept the live-cell imaging data (Figure 1F).

Agreement on claims C29-C32 regarding inverse relationship between Swi4 and Ime1. OpenEval focuses on these specific claims, while peer review groups them with broader downstream consequences (C2-C3, C33-C37). Both accept the immunoblotting and imaging data.

Agreement on claims C33-C35 regarding transcriptional consequences of SWI4 overexpression. OpenEval evaluates these separately while peer review groups them with other downstream effects. Both accept the mRNA-seq and GSEA data (Figure 2F-G).

Agreement on claims C36-C37 regarding meiotic entry defect validation. OpenEval evaluates these separately while peer review groups them with broader downstream consequences. Both accept the live-cell imaging and sporulation efficiency data.

Agreement on claims C2-C3 regarding consequences of SBF misregulation. OpenEval evaluates these as summary claims while peer review groups them with specific experimental results (C29-C37). Both find the evidence convincing.

Perfect agreement on claims C39-C42 regarding G1 cyclins as downstream effectors. Both explicitly acknowledge that CLN1/CLN2 mutations rescue the SWI4 overexpression phenotype, establishing causal link between cyclins and meiotic defect.

Agreement on claims C44-C47 regarding G1 cyclin overexpression inhibiting meiotic entry. OpenEval evaluates C43-C47 together while peer review groups C44-C47 with mechanism claims (C4, C50-C56, C81). Both accept the sporulation and imaging data.
Agreement on claim C43 (wild-type sporulation efficiency baseline). OpenEval groups this with C44-C47 while peer review treats it as a control measurement. Both accept this as valid baseline data.

Agreement on claims C50-C51 regarding insufficiency of rescuing IME1 expression alone. OpenEval evaluates C48-C51 together while peer review groups C50-C51 with broader mechanism (C4, C44-C47, C52-C56, C81). Both accept the evidence.

Agreement on claims C48-C49 regarding IME1 expression and Ime1 protein levels under cyclin overexpression. OpenEval groups these with C50-C51 while peer review evaluates them separately as supporting measurements. Both accept the RT-qPCR and immunoblotting data.

Agreement on claims C52-C54 regarding insufficiency of rescuing Ime1 nuclear localization. OpenEval evaluates these separately while peer review groups them with broader mechanism claims. Both accept the sporulation and imaging data.

Strong agreement on claims C4, C55-C56, C81 regarding cyclin-mediated disruption of Ime1-Ume6 interaction. Both explicitly acknowledge the nanobody tethering rescue as strong evidence for the mechanism. Peer review states 'Ime1 activity is antagonized by Swi4, and more specifically its interaction with Ume6.'

Agreement on claims C57-C60 regarding inverse expression of SWI4 transcript isoforms. OpenEval evaluates these separately while peer review groups them with broader LUTI mechanism (C5, C61-C69, C79). Both accept the RNA-seq and smFISH data.

Agreement on claims C61-C62 regarding functional consequence of LUTI deletion on Swi4 protein levels. OpenEval evaluates these separately while peer review groups them with broader LUTI mechanism. Both accept the RNA and immunoblotting data.

Agreement on claims C63-C65 regarding uORF-mediated translational repression. OpenEval evaluates these separately while peer review groups them with broader LUTI mechanism. Both accept the immunoblotting and RNA blotting data.

Agreement on claims C66-C67 regarding Ime1-dependent Swi4 downregulation. OpenEval evaluates these separately while peer review groups them with broader LUTI mechanism. Both accept the inducible IME1 experimental design.

Agreement on claims C68-C69 regarding Ime1-Ume6 regulation of SWI4LUTI. OpenEval evaluates these separately while peer review groups them with broader LUTI mechanism. Both accept the ChIP-seq and mRNA-seq data from published datasets.

Agreement on claims C5, C79 regarding LUTI-based regulation as main conclusion. OpenEval groups these with C6, C80 (dual mechanism) while peer review focuses on LUTI mechanism (C5, C57-C69, C79). Both accept this as a key finding.

Agreement on claims C70, C72 regarding insufficiency of single mechanisms. OpenEval evaluates these separately while peer review groups them with dual mechanism claims (C6, C71, C73-C78, C80). Both accept the mRNA-seq data.

Agreement on claims C73-C75 regarding redundancy and combined effect of regulatory mechanisms. OpenEval evaluates these separately while peer review groups them with broader dual mechanism. Both accept the mRNA-seq and GSEA data.

Agreement on claims C76-C78 regarding functional validation of redundant mechanisms. OpenEval evaluates these separately while peer review groups them with broader dual mechanism. Both accept the live-cell imaging data.

Agreement on claims C6, C80 regarding dual regulatory mechanism as main conclusion. OpenEval groups these with C5, C79 while peer review focuses on dual mechanism (C6, C70-C78, C80). Both accept this as a key finding with reviewer stating 'Whi5 restrict SBF activity during meiotic entry.'

Agreement on claim C71 regarding Whi5 nuclear localization during meiotic entry. OpenEval evaluates this as basis for investigating Whi5's role while peer review groups it with dual mechanism. Both accept the imaging data.

Agreement on claims C1, C7-C16, C82-C83 regarding background information on cell cycle and meiosis. OpenEval groups these with additional background claims (C84-C114) while peer review focuses on SBF-Ime1 framework. Both accept these as established facts.

Agreement on claims C84-C114 regarding additional background information. OpenEval groups these with C1, C7-C16, C82-C83 while peer review groups them with C38, C115-C119. Both accept these literature-based contextual claims without challenge.

Agreement on claim C38 regarding prior work on CLN1/CLN2. OpenEval evaluates this as context for current study while peer review groups it with broader background. Both accept this citation to Colomina et al., 1999.

Agreement on claim C117 regarding methodological limitations of prior work. OpenEval evaluates this as critical evaluation providing context while peer review groups it with background. Both accept this assessment of Colomina et al., 1999.

Agreement on claims C118-C119 regarding potential mechanisms for future investigation. OpenEval evaluates these as discussion points while peer review groups them with background. Both accept these observations from prior work.

Agreement on claims C115-C116 regarding gene ontology analysis. OpenEval evaluates these as providing functional context while peer review groups them with background. Both accept this analysis of mRNA-seq data without concerns.

Perfect agreement on claims C120-C122 regarding technical details. Both treat these as straightforward methodological descriptions that support the LUTI-based regulatory mechanism. No concerns raised by either evaluation.
